1.w: The one who stiffens his neck after numerous rebukes will suddenly be destroyed without remedy.

2.w: When the righteous become numerous, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.

3.w: The man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but whoever associates with prostitutes wastes his wealth.

4.w: A king brings stability to a land by justice, but one who exacts tribute tears it down.

5.w: The one who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his steps.

6.w: In the transgression of an evil person there is a snare, but a righteous person can sing and rejoice.

7.w: The righteous person cares for the legal rights of the poor; the wicked person does not understand such knowledge.

8.w: Scornful people inflame a city, but those who are wise turn away wrath.

9.w: When a wise person goes to court with a foolish person, there is no peace whether he is angry or laughs.

10.w: Bloodthirsty people hate someone with integrity; as for the upright, they seek his life.

11.w: A fool lets fly with all his temper, but a wise person keeps it back.

12.w: If a ruler listens to lies, all his ministers will be wicked.

13.w: The poor person and the oppressor have this in common: The Lord gives light to the eyes of them both.

14.w: If a king judges the poor in truth, his throne will be established forever.

15.w: A rod and reproof impart wisdom, but a child who is unrestrained brings shame to his mother.

16.w: When the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.

17.w: Discipline your child, and he will give you rest; he will bring you happiness.

18.w: When there is no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint, but the one who keeps the law, blessed is he!

19.w: A servant cannot be corrected by words, for although he understands, there is no answer.

20.w: You have seen someone who is hasty in his words — there is more hope for a fool than for him.

21.w: If someone pampers his servant from youth, he will be a weakling in the end.

22.w: An angry person stirs up dissension, and a wrathful person is abounding in transgression.

23.w: A person’s pride will bring him low, but one who has a lowly spirit will gain honor.

24.w: Whoever shares with a thief is his own enemy; he hears the oath to testify, but does not talk.

25.w: The fear of people becomes a snare, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be set on high.

26.w: Many people seek the face of a ruler, but it is from the Lord that one receives justice.

27.w: An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, and the one who lives an upright life is an abomination to the wicked.
